content: Participants in this study have the right to decide whether they want to participate or not. If they agree to participate, they can withdraw their consent at any time without facing any consequences or needing to provide a reason. If you have any questions about this research, you are encouraged to ask them freely. This study is being conducted by [name of lead institution] in collaboration with the Ministry of Health’s National Tuberculosis Programme and [collaborator name, Principal Investigator]. The research team will visit healthcare facilities that provide tuberculosis (TB) services to estimate the costs associated with delivering these services. The primary objective of this research is to develop a comprehensive set of unit costs for TB services in [country name]. The study involves a cross-sectional survey of [insert number of facilities] healthcare facilities in [country name], which have been selected through a two-stage stratified cluster sampling process. These facilities include both private (for-profit and non-profit) and public facilities at various service levels. Your facility is one of those selected for this study. The study will include interviews with key staff members (3 to 5 individuals) at your facility, reviews of relevant documents, observations of service delivery, and timesheets completed by some staff members. As a key staff member, we would like to ask you questions about the operational costs of providing TB services, the activities you are involved in, and the amount of time you dedicate to each activity. If you agree to participate, trained research assistants will conduct the following activities: They will ask you about your knowledge and experiences in managing TB patients, the training and supervision you have received, and the challenges you have faced in managing TB cases. They will review your facility’s project reports, financial records, and expenditure records, with your consent, to assess the types and quantities of inputs used in your clinical duties. They will observe you as you perform your daily clinical tasks to understand the time required for these activities. Observations will be conducted in a manner that respects patient privacy; for example, the research team will not be present during patient consultations but will record the duration of consultations from a common area adjacent to the consultation room. You will also be asked to complete a timesheet documenting your activities during working hours over the course of one week. There are no significant risks associated with participating in this study. The interview will take approximately 60 minutes, and the observations will be conducted over a working day. No audio or video recordings will be made during the interview or observations, but detailed notes will be taken. All responses and observations will be treated with strict confidentiality. If you feel uncertain about answering any questions, you are free to decline to answer. However, providing accurate responses is important for the success of the study. There are no direct personal benefits to participating in this study. However, your participation will contribute to improving the National Tuberculosis Programme’s services and help in planning its medium-term expenditures. The data collected may also assist other countries’ National TB Programmes in estimating the costs of their TB services and planning their resources more effectively. All study documents will be securely stored in locked cabinets and on password-protected computers. Your questionnaire will not include your name, ensuring that your responses remain anonymous. Information about your workload and the resources typically used in providing TB services will be aggregated into a total estimate of the unit cost per TB episode. The findings from this research will be shared in summary form, without revealing individual identities, with participating facilities, the National Tuberculosis Programme, collaborating institutions, and the broader scientific community through policy briefs and scientific publications. Anonymized data collected during this study will also be shared with the Global Health Cost Consortium (GHCC) to improve cost extrapolations across different settings. The cost data from this project will be incorporated into the web-based GHCC platform. This research has been approved by several institutional, national, and international committees to ensure that it is important, relevant to [country name], and adheres to nationally and internationally agreed research guidelines. These committees also ensure that the safety and rights of all participants are respected. Participation in this research is entirely voluntary. You are free to decide whether or not to participate. If you agree to participate, you can withdraw at any time without any consequences or the need to provide a reason. If you have any questions about this research, you are encouraged to ask them freely. By signing the consent form, you confirm that the study has been explained to you, that you understand the information provided, and that your questions have been answered satisfactorily. You will also confirm your agreement to participate in the interview, observational research, and completion of a working timesheet over one week. You understand that you can withdraw your consent at any time without any impact on you.
